title: Quarterly safety-lane: On‑prem compatibility cadence, experiment cohorts, and OKR signal radar
creator: Nora Patel
description: Objective: Define and deliver a repeatable quarterly cadence ('safety‑lane') that minimizes upgrade and compatibility risk for on‑prem / VPC customers while progressing OKRs for Private deployments. This ticket scopes the playbook, the experiment cohort criteria, automated compatibility checks, and the monitoring/telemetry signals that gate rollouts to different cohorts. The playbook must support dark launches, rollback gates, and a set of 'acceptance smoke tests' that run in customer-like environments before activation. Emphasis on measurable signals so product and engineering can objectively greenlight each tranche.
success_metrics: <20% integration regressions caught post-activation vs previous quarter
Time to detect a compat regression <= 45 minutes via new telemetry
>80% of cohort customers successfully upgraded in canary wave without manual interventions
Clear OKR alignment: private-onprem stability metric improved by 15% quarter-over-quarter
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc (Confluence) drafted with step-by-step cadence and roles
Automated compatibility test suite integrated into pre-activation pipeline
Cohort selection rubric finalized and signed off by GTM/Support
Telemetry dashboard (Console) with rollout SLOs and regression alerts configured
Runbook for rollback and emergency rollback exercise completed in staging
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dark-launch against synthetic environments (2 weeks). Phase 1: Canary cohort (5 customers) with enhanced telemetry and a single-tranche activation (3 weeks). Phase 2: Staged cohort expansion (up to 25 customers) with automated acceptance gates (4 weeks). Phase 3: Broad activation with scheduled windows and post-activation audit (ongoing). Each phase requires green signals for latency, error-rate, config drift, and KV-cache integrity. If any gate fails, revert to previous model/variant and trigger incident runbook.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer environments vary widely leading to unanticipated failures — Mitigation: expand synthetic environment matrix and require a minimal compatibility shim for known vendor configurations
Risk: Telemetry blind spots delay detection — Mitigation: add heartbeat + KV-check probes and pre-configured dashboards before cohort activation
Risk: Rollback complexity for stateful on‑prem tenants — Mitigation: pre-validated rollback steps and a staged snapshot/restore checklist
Risk: Resource contention with Dedicated capacity work — Mitigation: cross-team capacity booking and 'no-conflict' windows in calendar
implementation_notes: Prioritize integration contract tests for network policy, KMS access patterns, and upgrade sequencing. Runtime team to deliver a small 'compatibility shim' binary that performs preflight checks; SRE to own the alert playbook. Avoid large schema changes during this cadence; use translation layer where necessary. Quantization/version fallbacks should be included as a last-resort automatic mitigation.
